feed.title: Combined summary - Towards New Self-Custody Best Practices

entry.title: Combined summary - Towards New Self-Custody Best Practices
entry.summary: The recent vulnerabilities exposed in hardware wallets like Coldcard, which led to significant financial losses, underline the critical need for robust self-custody practices within the Bitcoin community. A notable issue was the low-entropy vulnerability that resulted in losses exceeding $100 million. To mitigate such risks, it is recommended to adopt a 2-of-2 multisig setup utilizing hardware from different vendors to avoid common-mode failures, which could arise from shared cryptographic libraries like secp256k1. In terms of managing seed phrases, an innovative approach involves users selecting 11 out of the 12 BIP39 words themselves from a mixed bag or other randomized methods, ensuring they generate and verify their entropy manually. This method circumvents the shortcomings of hardware-generated entropy and allows for a more verifiable assurance of randomness. However, the 12th word should be chosen by the wallet software to maintain the integrity of the checksum. For backup best practices, durable materials such as steel or titanium plates are advocated for punching in the seed words, thereby providing a resilient medium against physical degradation. Furthermore, operational security during transactions is crucial. Users are advised to perform small test transactions to confirm the accuracy of the receive addresses and the transaction amounts on their hardware devices. This step is essential to ensure the devices are not compromised. Additionally, the practice of storing backup devices and seeds in separate, secure locations is emphasized to minimize the risk of total loss should one location be compromised. Lastly, there is an acknowledgment of the varying needs of users ranging from everyday transactions to life savings, suggesting a tiered approach to security might be appropriate. This would tailor the complexity of the security setup to the value being protected and encourage practices like recovery rehearsals before moving substantial funds into a new wallet setup. The discussion also highlights the potential benefits of integrating checksum correction functionalities directly into hardware devices to aid users in manual seed generation processes, thereby enhancing user confidence and security in self-managed wallets.
